commands.notes: GNU xargs: empty input runs COMMAND once with no items unless -r (or -I, which runs per line). Default echo, blank/newline splitting with quote/backslash grammar; -0 exact NUL items, -d one delimiter byte (C escapes allowed) with no quote grammar. -I one input line per batch, replacing the placeholder in arguments; -L N nonblank lines per batch; -n N items per batch. Batches run in input order, -P N at most min(N, concurrent_processes) at once (0 means the bound); output of each batch is delivered in input order. -t prints each command line to stderr first. Each batch is its own bound child; input never becomes program text. BSD -J R replaces one whole argument R with the batch's items; -E/-e EOF stops input at a logical EOF item; GNU -i[R] and -l[N] are -I R (default {}) and -L N (default 1); -s caps each command line's bytes; -x refuses a batch that does not fit; -o is accepted, as children never read a terminal.
